# Familiar Therapeutics Launches with $5 Million Seed to Close the Gap Between Human and Veterinary Medicine

Updated Thu, October 22, 2026 at 12:12 PM UTC

0

Image

REDWOOD CITY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct 22, 2026--

Familiar Therapeutics launched today with $5 million in seed funding to bring the advances of modern human medicine to dogs and cats. The round was led by Pioneer Fund, Icehouse Ventures and BreakTHRU, a syndicate of animal-health industry leaders and veterinarians, with participation from angel investors.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261022813367/en/

Over the past two decades, a new generation of medicines has changed the outlook for people with chronic and life-threatening diseases. Dogs and cats develop many of the same diseases as people, often driven by the same underlying biology, yet very little of that medical progress has reached them. Fewer than 10 new drugs are approved by the FDA each year for companion animals, compared with more than 50 for people. For many serious conditions, veterinarians still rely on human medicines used off-label, without dosing or safety data for the species. Much of the science needed to change this exists, but adapting a drug for animals takes its own clinical studies, manufacturing work and FDA review. Without a dedicated path for that work, promising medicines rarely make it across to dogs and cats.

Familiar was built to close that gap. Because each program starts with years of human research behind it, Familiar aims to bring disease-modifying medicines to pets significantly faster than the seven to ten years a new animal drug typically takes. The company works with pharmaceutical and biotech partners on each program, licensing the veterinary rights to their drugs and leading the clinical development and manufacturing work needed for FDA approval in dogs and cats.

In the five months since its founding, Familiar built a pipeline of four lead programs and nine earlier-stage programs for dogs and cats, signed multiple partnership and licensing agreements with biopharmaceutical companies, opened two investigational new animal drug (INAD) files with the FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine and filed one provisional patent. The seed funding will move its lead programs into clinical studies and advance the rest of its pipeline.

Familiar was founded by serial entrepreneurs Elizabeth Iorns, PhD, and Dan Knox, MBA. They previously co-founded Science Exchange, the Y Combinator-backed R&D outsourcing platform used by the world's largest pharmaceutical companies, and led it through its acquisition in 2024. The gap between human and veterinary medicine became personal for Elizabeth in 2020, when her French Bulldog, Lily, was diagnosed with a terminal brain tumor. dan@familiartx.com

Image: Familiar launches with $5M seed to bring human drugs to dogs and cats

What's the deal? Familiar Therapeutics launched with $5 million in seed funding to adapt advances in human medicine for dogs and cats. The round was led by Pioneer Fund, Icehouse Ventures, and BreakTHRU, with participation from angel investors.

What's the endgame? Familiar licenses the veterinary rights to drugs already backed by years of human research, then leads the clinical development and manufacturing needed for FDA approval in pets. Because each program starts with that human data, the company aims to move faster than the seven to ten years a new animal drug typically takes.

Why now? Fewer than 10 new drugs are approved by the FDA each year for companion animals, compared with more than 50 for people. For many serious conditions, vets still rely on human medicines used off-label, without dosing or safety data for the species.

In five months, Familiar has built 13 programs across oncology, neurology, cardiology, respiratory disease, and immunology; signed multiple licensing agreements; opened two investigational new animal drug files with the FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine; and filed one provisional patent. Its first clinical study is set to open at the University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital this fall. The seed will move its lead programs into clinical studies.

Who's behind it? Familiar was founded by Elizabeth Iorns and Dan Knox, who previously co-founded Science Exchange, the Y Combinator-backed R&D outsourcing platform, and led it through a 2024 acquisition. "Our goal is to give vets proven, FDA-approved treatments that change the course of serious diseases in dogs and cats, where today they often have very few options," said Iorns.

The signal: Investor interest in veterinary therapeutics is widening from pet-care products toward drug development, with Loyal raising $100 million in February and Gamgee $4 million in August. Familiar's human-to-veterinary translation thesis stands out, but the seed is an early signal — its scientific and commercial case will depend on its specific candidates and results.

# Familiar Therapeutics Launches With $5 Million In Seed Funding

By Amit Chowdhry Yesterday at 4:16 PM

Familiar Therapeutics Launches With $5 Million In Seed Funding

Familiar Therapeutics, a Redwood City, California-based biotechnology company developing treatments for companion animals, has launched with $5 million in seed funding to adapt advances in human medicine for dogs and cats. The financing was led by Pioneer Fund, Icehouse Ventures, and BreakTHRU, an investment syndicate comprising animal health industry leaders and veterinarians, with additional participation from angel investors.

Founded in May 2026 by entrepreneurs Elizabeth Iorns and Dan Knox, Familiar is developing a portfolio of veterinary medicines based on drugs that have already undergone substantial research for human diseases.

The company aims to address the gap between advances in human therapeutics and the limited treatment options available for pets suffering from serious illnesses.

Although dogs and cats can develop many of the same diseases as humans, relatively few new medications are approved specifically for companion animals each year. Familiar noted that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approves fewer than 10 new companion animal drugs annually, compared with more than 50 for human use.

As a result, veterinarians frequently rely on medications developed for humans, sometimes without comprehensive dosing or safety data specific to the animal species being treated.

Familiar intends to address this challenge by licensing veterinary rights to promising treatments from pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, then conducting the animal-specific research, manufacturing development, and regulatory work required for veterinary approval.

By building on existing human research, the company believes it can accelerate development compared with the seven to ten years typically required to bring a new animal medicine to market.

# Transcripta Bio Announces Scientific Advisory Board to Advance High-Certainty Drug Discovery

September 23, 2026 | 

5 min read

  * Twitter
  * LinkedIn
  * Facebook
  * Email
  * Print

Leaders in human genetics, transcriptomic biology, clinical drug development, and neuromuscular clinical trial design to help guide Transcripta's pipeline

PALO ALTO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Transcripta Bio, an AI-powered drug discovery company focused on neurological and neuromuscular diseases, today announced additions to its Scientific Advisory Board (SAB). The SAB includes leaders with expertise in human genetics, transcriptomic biology, clinical drug development, and neuromuscular clinical trial design.

The SAB will help guide Transcripta's scientific and clinical strategy as the company advances its pipeline toward the clinic, drawing on its closed-loop discovery engine. The engine uses transcriptomic signature matching to identify drug candidates whose molecular profiles are the inverse of patient-derived disease signatures. The platform combines a Disease Signature Atlas built from patient single-cell RNA sequencing data, a Drug-Gene Atlas mapping the full transcriptomic response of clinically tested and novel compounds, and Conductor AI, a machine learning system trained on more than one billion gene responses.

The SAB members are:

  * Anthony Accorsi, Ph.D. | Venture Partner, Blackbird Laboratories
A former Head of Muscle Biology at ReNAgade Therapeutics and Fulcrum Therapeutics as well as currently serving as CSO of NuGate Therapeutics, Dr. Accorsi has driven programs from gene target to IND across multiple modalities and diseases — bridging human genetics and druggable biology for Transcripta's pipeline.

  * Matt Deardorff, M.D., Ph.D. | Professor at University of Southern California and Director of Personalized Care at Children's Hospital Los Angeles
A clinical geneticist and molecular biologist, Dr. Deardorff has spent the last 20+ years identifying and investigating the genetic and cell biological basis of a number of rare disorders of syndromic intellectual disability. Currently, as the Director of Personalized Care at the Children’s Hospital of Los Angeles, he is passionate about applying genomic medicine to pediatric care and increasing therapeutic options for children with rare disorders.

Authors: Bryce Bolin, Leo Alcorn, Max Brodheim, Alexa Gordon, Lordrick Kahinga, Michael Lundquist, Rita Morris, J. Xavier Prochaska
Date: Thu Oct 15 17:58:04 2026

We characterize comet P/2026 N2, whose outer Main Belt orbit has $a=3.07$ au, $e=0.21$, and $i=2.25^\circ$, using optical observations, archival imaging, and dynamical integrations. Observations from the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) at NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory in 2026 June-July and Keck/LRIS imaging on October 7 show active morphology across perihelion over 102 days. Within a projected aperture radius of approximately 1,000 km, Keck colors of $g-r=0.50\pm0.05$ and $r-i=0.06\pm0.06$ mag are consistent with nearly neutral B/C-complex reflectance. Phase-corrected $a(0^\circ)fρ=3.66\pm0.12$ cm in derived $r$ and $3.46\pm0.17$ cm in $i$ are comparable to LSST measurements. The geometry-corrected $i$-band aperture brightness changes by $0.07\pm0.07$ mag between July 9 and October 7; the 2,000 km $r$-band aperture measurements are also consistent between epochs. These results support sustained observable activity, consistent with prolonged or recurrent dust production. Archival DECam images recover N2 on 2021 July 4, but its activity state is inconclusive. A 5,000-particle forward integration retains a concentrated outer Main Belt core throughout 50 Myr. We hypothesize that volatile sublimation, possibly of water ice, sustains activity near perihelion.

Title: PRET is a few-shot system for pan-cancer recognition without example training
Authors: Yi Li, Ziyu Ning, Tianqi Xiang, Qixiang Zhang, Zhihao Lin, Min Yi, Feiyan Feng, Baozhen Zeng, Xuexia Qian, Lu Sun, Jiace Qin, Ling Xiang, Chao Fan, Tian Qin, Qian Wang, Xiu-Wu Bian, Kun-Hsing Yu, Kang Zhang, Qingling Zhang, Xiaomeng Li

Pathological examination stands as the cornerstone in cancer diagnosis, impacting millions worldwide annually. With the shortage of pathologists globally, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged rapidly to automate the diagnostics process. However, conventional AI models require substantial labeled data for each disease, posing huge challenges in scalability and practicality. Therefore, we introduce PRET (pan-cancer recognition without examples training), a few-shot system to achieve flexible, scalable, and effective cancer recognition across diverse organs, hospitals and tasks without training. Evaluated on 23 international benchmarks comprising 4,484 whole-slide images, our method outperforms existing approaches across 20 tasks, achieving over 97% area under the curve on 15 benchmarks with a maximum improvement of 36.76%. Notably, PRET delivers clinical-grade diagnostic performance in lymph node metastasis detection using only eight slide examples, outperforming 11 pathologists. By offering a flexible and cost-effective solution for pan-cancer recognition, PRET paves the way for accessible and equitable AI-based pathology systems, particularly benefiting minority populations and underserved regions.

Title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
Authors: Dongxu Yang, Hongda Yan, Renxin Wang, Baoli Zhang, Haojia Zuo, Ying Zhao, Youmin Chen, Xiaojian Liao, Congming Gao, Tianyang Jiang, Yixiao Chen, Qing Wang, Zhiguo Yu, Xiaqing Li, Yuhao Zhang, Jiawen Sun, Renzhe Xu, De Mi, Tiancheng Wu, Xianya Fu, Xuanlu Zhao, Bo Feng, Meixuan Ren, Guanming Lin, Ziheng Zhou, Xinhua Wang

Existing agent benchmarks typically evaluate agents on well-specified tasks defined by issue reports, specifications, or task tickets. Real-world customer delivery is different: forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) must clarify ambiguous requirements, work in live systems, and uncover unstated constraints. We introduce FDE-Gym, a benchmark of 95 end-to-end delivery tasks from 20 customer scenarios across 18 sectors, each adapted by industry experts from real-world delivery projects. In simulated customer environments with scripted stakeholders and modifiable customer systems, agents interact with stakeholders and operate on production-like systems to deliver working solutions. FDE-Gym scores a delivery by how much it improves the customer's own success metric, normalized between 0 (unchanged system) and 1 (reference solution), with penalties for stakeholder interactions (messages, trial runs, and waiting time). An online platform lets humans practice FDE skills under the same grading criteria. We evaluate 13 model configurations from seven providers. In the realistic setting, where unstated constraints must be discovered, the best configuration achieves a mean FDE-Gym score of 0.56 and resolves only 14 of the 95 tasks (a score of at least 0.8 with no incident). Discovering unstated constraints is the primary bottleneck: performance drops sharply when models must uncover them without explicit guidance. Yet information discovery alone does not account for the gap: even on the 23 tasks where the best configuration obtains every key fact from stakeholders, it reaches a normalized business uplift of 0.8 or above on only 10. These results reveal a substantial gap between solving well-specified tasks and delivering effective AI systems for real customers.
